notes.title: Version 1.0
notes.notes:
1.0 might suggest this is the first release, but in fact the game has gone thru at least 10 public version bumps since going live on steam as early access.  It should be rock-solid at this point. If it's on your wish-list now is the time to buy!

This version bings small changes, the most visible being new fonts rather than the Arial knock-off that's the engine default up to now.

notes.title: Rebinding! Now, is there anything else left to do?
notes.notes:
The final thing I've been wanting to add before leaving early access is a rebinding implementation.  Now, it's done: gamepad buttons and keyboard buttons can be bound to actions like jump or set checkpoint. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45202140/7eddbffdd17be235d790617bea8014603ec74eda.png[/img]

There's really no other excuse to keep this early access, but as it's a major feature change that touches multiple areas I'm going to hold off for a few days in case of bug reports.

notes.title: fixed level 39 achievement and new lighting
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45202140/d4b7789bc7eda378d1c4f30e04e946f8b07d2282.png[/img]Bug fix: level 39 achievement is now gettable (just finish the level).

Experimenting with different lighting for the two "outside the game" levels to further delineate alien levels vs scientist levels (tutorial + science lab). Subtle, mostly just an excuse to experiment with softer lighting models.

notes.title: Final build before leaving early access?
notes.notes:
The Game is nearly ready to leave early access. To my knowledge all levels are finished, all bugs squashed, and all achievements ready to be achieved.  

And...  The Science Lab is no longer "under construction"! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45202140/8276586dfe9637acedb1e16a4807a89012cf68f2.png[/img]

Consider this a dry run for leaving early access - one last chance to catch any problems before the full weight of Steam's player base is directed at the game on launch - at least for the 5 minutes or so that it will get top billing on the new release list (after which some other game will be even newer).

notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45202140/44f3a57b091ab7f6f26442642bfd7d11c34ad948.png[/img]Minor change: instructions now use gamepad (or keyboard, as appropriate) icons when describing how to jump, set checkpoints, etc.

notes.title: Epilogue finished and ready for the public
notes.notes:
The game has 32 (or 34 depending on how you count) regular levels, with a complete story ark told over that series of levels.

After that, there's mostly just speed running challenges. BUT in order to provide some reward for the speed runners, there are 5 additional levels and a followup story line / grand conclusion that can only be unlocked by speed running. I call this the Epilogue. It is now finished and part of the game. Lucky, since the game releases tomorrow (Dec 4th).

If you aren't into speed running but feel like you are missing out to not get to the epilogue, I feel you. But our speed running challenges are fairly mild, and more about finding the most optimal path, not split-second timing. So you might enjoy them despite yourself. And there's rumors of a way to bypass some of the speed running challenges, even...

PS if you are into speed running in a hard-core kind of way, you can always compete on the world leaderboard for each level. Being the best in the world won't unlock any extra content, but it might be fun, and isn't that the best kind of content?

notes.title: Now with leaderboards
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45202140/d7d049bd439bc9fa19151fd08ecda5e169cf87f0.png[/img]

Steam leaderboards have been added so you can compare you times (any % [i]and [/i]100%) against the global top 10. Which right now is just me, and in order to not make it too challenging, I've intentionally only submitted a few slower run times, for a few levels. 

At least that's my cover story.

Check out the Science Lab level to see leaderboards for every level that you've finished.

PS. the game is not *just* about speed running. It's an option. Seriously, go slow if you want. In fact, I'm torn about printing the best global times every time you finish a level. I don't want casual chillaxing players to feel like they aren't doing it right. I just want to fully support the people who want the extra challenge (and, admittedly, the collectable layout is partially designed for speed running).

So here's the question: should I print out the global ranking on the level end screen too, or only in the science lab?

notes.title: Small fix, big effect?
notes.notes:
I've always been adamant that invert Y camera was the only way to play, so much so that I made it the default in my game. But of course I realize that I'm in the minority, so the very first thing you do in the tutorial is decide if you want to use invert Y or "normal" camera controls (shades of the first Halo, or Ratchet Deadlocked).

A new player, however, discovered that this leads to a significant ambiguity for what it means to select "invert y" in the tutorial; does that mean invert the current controls? 

No, they are already inverted! So selecting Invert Y does nothing. Which in retrospect is definitely confusing to everybody but me, and may have already earned the game it's first negative review. So now the game defaults to non-inverted Y; a change of exactly 1 character to the source code. 

Thanks, *semi-anonymous* steam player!

Literature Cited

https://steamcommunity.com/app/3177810/discussions/0/4631484289352000570/

notes.title: Release delayed until after TG sale
notes.notes:
At the advice of Steam the game will go live a little later than expected, Dec 4th, rather than this week. The reason is boringly practical: the game will be hidden under the thanksgiving/late November sale and won't even be shown as a "new release" if I put it out now. 

So, we wait.

But, if you just can't wait (I'm looking *just* at you, Carl), you can still back my kickstarter for a pre-release key reward. 

Meanwhlie, this will allow a little more fine-tuning of the achievement difficulty.

notes.title: Nearing release!
notes.notes:
We've been crash free / bug free for over a month, and all but the final level are fully polished. I think it's almost time to release my baby into the world!

Final tuning of the game is all that remains, Looking forward to seeing what achievements are easy and what are (too?) hard.
